newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BankWest sees growth from eastern states.
newsitem.headline: BankWest sees growth from eastern states.

text.p: Perth-based regional bank Bank of Western Australia Ltd (BankWest) said on Wednesday it saw its best growth opportunities in the eastern states of Australia, namely in New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria.
Asked if the bank had reached a market share ceiling in Western Australia (currently 24 percent), the bank's managing director, Warwick Kent said: "Probably yes."
"Future growth will come from interstate and from housing loans, commercial banking and equipment finance," he said.
BankWest operates its interstate business largely through agencies.
The banks' Australian assets outside of Western Australia have grown to 16.9 percent of its total assets from 13.4 percent in the previous year.

BankWest, 51.47 percent owned by the Bank of Scotland, earlier announced an A$94.5 million profit for the year to end-February compared with its prospectus forecast of a profit of A$100.2 million. The bank warned in February that results were likely to be five percent below the forecast.
"Our future strategic focus is likely to remain unchanged. We are outting a great effort into growing our direct banking operations not only interstate but also in W.A.," he said.
Kent said he expected the next movement in official cash rates to be up, but not for several months and maybe not until 1998.
